articles.title: Mother of Three Walks Out With Alleged Lover, Husband Breaks Down at Police Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bengaluru (Karnataka): A family dispute under Bannerghatta police limits (Anekal taluk) has sparked debate after a video surfaced showing a father weeping for his wife’s return while holding her saree at the police station.

body.html:
Bengaluru (Karnataka): A family dispute under Bannerghatta police limits (Anekal taluk) has sparked debate after a video surfaced showing a father weeping for his wife’s return while holding her saree at the police station.

Police said Manjunath, a resident of Basavapura village, married Leelavathi 11 years ago and has two sons and a daughter. For nearly two years, Leelavathi allegedly maintained a relationship with Santosh, a car driver.

On 31 August, Leelavathi reportedly left home with Santosh, prompting Manjunath to lodge a complaint seeking her return. Officers traced the pair and brought them to the station, counselling Leelavathi to reconsider for the sake of her three children.

However, Leelavathi refused reconciliation, allegedly removed her thali (mangalsutra), and chose to leave with Santosh, declaring she no longer wished to live with Manjunath or care for the children.

Footage from the station shows the couple’s weeping children and Manjunath pleading, holding his wife’s saree as she walks away. The video has gone viral, triggering emotional reactions across social media.

articles.title: Wife and Lover Held for Killing husband, Police Say ‘Drama’ Exposed by Call Records
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Sultanpur (U.P.): Police in the Chanda area of Sultanpur district have arrested Puja and her alleged lover Jaiprakash alias Dangar Yadav for the murder of her husband Mahesh Kumar, a daily wage worker recently returned from Ludhiana.

body.html:
Sultanpur (U.P.): Police in the Chanda area of Sultanpur district have arrested Puja and her alleged lover Jaiprakash alias Dangar Yadav for the murder of her husband Mahesh Kumar, a daily wage worker recently returned from Ludhiana.

Mahesh’s throat-slit body was discovered on 4 September in Kindipur market. Puja was seen weeping bitterly near the corpse, initially convincing villagers it was an attack by unknown assailants.

Investigators, however, traced frequent phone calls between Puja and Jaiprakash on the day of the killing. Under interrogation, Jaiprakash reportedly admitted he plied Mahesh with liquor, after which Puja joined him; Jaiprakash allegedly slit Mahesh’s throat with a knife while Puja struck his chest with a brick.

Police recovered the knife, brick, and mobile phone used in the crime. Both accused have been remanded to jail, and further legal proceedings are underway.

Mahesh, 38, had been supporting the family through labour work in Punjab and had only returned home earlier this year.

articles.title: Lucknow Campus Shock: Law Student Slapped 20 Times in 90 Seconds, Video Sparks Outrage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Lucknow (U.P.): A disturbing case of ragging-style assault has surfaced at a private university, where a law student was allegedly slapped over 20 times by two classmates inside a car parked on campus.

body.html:
Lucknow (U.P.): A disturbing case of ragging-style assault has surfaced at a private university, where a law student was allegedly slapped over 20 times by two classmates inside a car parked on campus.

The viral video shows the victim forced to sit silently while a boy and a girl repeatedly strike him, warning him not to shield his face or face “more beating.” The incident lasted roughly 90 seconds and has reportedly left the student traumatised and skipping classes.

In the footage, one assailant can be heard saying, “Would you dare speak about the character of Jahnavi and Saumya?” The motive for the attack remains unclear.

University officials and police are expected to verify the video and investigate. The clip’s rapid spread online has triggered public anger and calls for strict action against the perpetrators.

articles.title: Pilibhit Shock: Samosa Dispute Spirals Into Brawl, Panchayat Assault Leaves Family Injured
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Pilibhit (U.P.): In a bizarre turn of events, a simple demand for samosas led to a violent family clash in Puranpur, Uttar Pradesh. Police said Sangeeta, newly married to Shivam, asked him on 29 August to bring samosas.

body.html:
Pilibhit (U.P.): In a bizarre turn of events, a simple demand for samosas led to a violent family clash in Puranpur, Uttar Pradesh.

Police said Sangeeta, newly married to Shivam, asked him on 29 August to bring samosas. Shivam reportedly lost his money en route and returned empty-handed, sparking an argument. Sangeeta refused dinner and summoned her relatives, who allegedly assaulted Shivam.

According to Shivam, his mother was also beaten by his brother-in-law. Matters worsened during a village panchayat at ex-pradhan Awadhesh Sharma’s house, where Sangeeta’s relatives allegedly attacked Shivam’s family with belts, leaving several injured.

A video of the incident has since gone viral, fuelling online debate over domestic disputes turning violent. Police have registered a case against the accused and launched an investigation.

Circle Officer Prateek Dahiya confirmed: “On 29 August, a fight broke out between two parties. A complaint has been filed and an injured youth is under treatment.”

articles.title: Agra Shock: Man Found Bound in Car Trunk After Family Dispute, Police Rescue Amid Scuffle
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Agra (U.P.): A dramatic case of domestic discord turned violent unfolded in Kheria village, Khandauli, where a man was rescued from the trunk of a car after being allegedly abducted and tied up by his brothers-in-law.

body.html:
Agra (U.P.): A dramatic case of domestic discord turned violent unfolded in Kheria village, Khandauli, where a man was rescued from the trunk of a car after being allegedly abducted and tied up by his brothers-in-law.

Police said they intercepted the vehicle near Padraw village on the Agra–Hathras road after an alert was raised. On opening the trunk, officers found Hardev Singh with his hands and feet bound, gagged with a cloth. A scuffle erupted between relatives and police before the situation was brought under control. Two suspects were taken into custody.

Hardev, who has been married to Lakshmi of Hathras for 25 years, alleged that her family has long been pressuring him over property, sparking repeated quarrels. He claimed that on Thursday morning, while he was praying, brothers-in-law Rajpal, Satyapal and Dharmveer, along with two others, tied him up and forced him into the car.

Rajpal disputed the charges, telling police that Hardev had severely beaten their sister, who needed hospitalisation, and that they were taking him to the police when he resisted.

A video of the incident, showing Hardev bound inside the trunk, has since gone viral. DCP (West) Atul Sharma confirmed there is a long-standing marital dispute. A case has been registered based on Hardev’s complaint, and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Ajit Pawar Sparks Row After Video Shows Him Rebuking IPS Officer Over Solapur Soil Mafia Action
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mumbai: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and NCP leader Ajit Pawar has landed in the eye of a storm after a viral video showed him sharply rebuking IPS officer Anjana Krishna during her crackdown on illegal murrum (soil) excavation in Solapur district.

body.html:
Mumbai: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and NCP leader Ajit Pawar has landed in the eye of a storm after a viral video showed him sharply rebuking IPS officer Anjana Krishna during her crackdown on illegal murrum (soil) excavation in Solapur district.

The clip, shot near Kurdu village, Madha tehsil, records Pawar saying, “I will take action against you… I am myself talking to you and you are asking me to call you directly… itna aapko daring hua hai kya (how dare you?).”

According to officials, Krishna was acting on complaints of illegal soil mining when local villagers resisted the police. NCP worker Baba Jagtap reportedly called Pawar and handed the phone to the officer, triggering the heated exchange.

The video’s circulation has sparked charges of political intimidation and shielding the soil mafia. Pawar later issued a statement saying his remarks were aimed at defusing tensions and not at interfering in law enforcement, adding he has the “highest respect for the police force and the rule of law.”

Maharashtra CM and Home Minister Devendra Fadnavis has not commented on the matter yet.
Meanwhile, NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule slammed the attack on Krishna’s credentials, calling it an “assault on constitutional guarantees and gender equality.”

The episode has ignited a debate over political pressure on police officers handling illegal mining rackets in the state.

articles.title: UPSC Aspirant Shot Dead Weeks After Inter-Caste Marriage: Hardoi Police Probe ‘Honour Killing’ Angle
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Hardoi (U.P.): The death of 24-year-old UPSC aspirant Manvi Mishra has triggered outrage after she was found with a gunshot wound at her family home.

body.html:
Hardoi (U.P.): The death of 24-year-old UPSC aspirant Manvi Mishra has triggered outrage after she was found with a gunshot wound at her family home.

Police first suspected suicide as a country-made pistol lay near the body, but inconsistencies surfaced: the wound was on the left side of her head while the firearm rested in her right hand.

Investigators learnt that Manvi had married Abhinav Katihar—an inter-caste union—on 7 January 2025, securing court registration and even High Court-ordered police protection against family threats. Her parents later persuaded her to return, promising a “proper Hindu wedding” post her brother’s marriage.

On 31 August, Abhinav’s calls went unanswered; hours later, police informed him of her death.

Detectives allege that during a confrontation, Manvi’s brother Ashutosh alias Veeru Mishra shot her, with help from their mother in staging it as suicide. Both have been arrested, and Veeru has confessed, police claim.

The case has reignited debate on honour-based violence in Uttar Pradesh, highlighting that even court protection cannot always shield young women from family backlash over self-chosen marriages.

articles.title: Lucknow Shock: Woman Alleges Assault by Dial-112 Police After Molestation Call
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Lucknow, UP: A disturbing case has surfaced at PGI area where a young woman claims she was beaten and humiliated by police after calling Dial-112 to report molestation. The incident occurred late Wednesday when she was heading to meet a friend in Sector-10.

body.html:
Lucknow, UP: A disturbing case has surfaced at PGI area where a young woman claims she was beaten and humiliated by police after calling Dial-112 to report molestation.

The incident occurred late Wednesday when she was heading to meet a friend in Sector-10. Two youths allegedly misbehaved with her, prompting her to seek police help. A team—led by a sub-inspector with two women constables—arrived but, according to the victim, dragged her into the vehicle, called her a “prostitute,” tore her clothes, and assaulted her at the outpost.

In a viral video, the woman accuses police of rubbing her face with shoes and threatening false intoxication charges, warning she may “commit suicide in front of the Legislative Assembly” if denied justice.

Lucknow Police state that ACP Gosaiganj is investigating, and legal action will follow based on findings.

articles.title: Gorakhpur Horror: Woman Gunned Down by Husband Outside Photo Studio
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Gorakhpur, UP: Panic gripped Jail Road in Shahpur on Wednesday night after a 30-year-old woman, Mamta Chauhan, was shot dead by her husband outside a photo studio around 8 p.m (03.09.2025) .

body.html:
Gorakhpur, UP: Panic gripped Jail Road in Shahpur on Wednesday night after a 30-year-old woman, Mamta Chauhan, was shot dead by her husband outside a photo studio around 8 p.m (03.09.2025) .

Eyewitnesses said the accused, Vishwakarma Chauhan, arrived on a motorcycle, argued with Mamta, then pulled a country-made pistol from his helmet and fired. He reportedly stood near the body for 25 minutes, repeating, “I was troubled by her,” until police detained him.

Locals rushed Mamta to Vinayak Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Police confirmed the couple had been married for 15 years but separated for over a year due to property disputes.

SHO Neeraj Rai said Vishwakarma is in custody and under interrogation. The killing has reignited debate on domestic violence and illegal firearms in Uttar Pradesh.

articles.title: Dead Rat in Paneer Sabzi: Badaun Dhaba Sparks Food Safety Uproar
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Badaun, UP: What began as a routine meal turned into shock when diners at Anmol Dhaba in Bilsi town found a dead rat in their paneer sabzi. The incident, which occurred on 27 August, has triggered outrage after a video of the rodent in the dish went viral on social media.

body.html:
Badaun, UP: What began as a routine meal turned into shock when diners at Anmol Dhaba in Bilsi town found a dead rat in their paneer sabzi. The incident, which occurred on 27 August, has triggered outrage after a video of the rodent in the dish went viral on social media.

Nishant Maheshwari and his friend Puneet, both residents of Bilsi, said they had eaten half the plate before noticing the carcass. They confronted the dhaba staff, who apologised and tried to settle the matter on the spot.

Sub-Divisional Magistrate Prem Pal Singh confirmed the administration has seen the video. Officials will collect food samples for testing, and checks on other eateries have been ordered. Bilsi Kotwal Manoj Kumar Singh stated no formal complaint has yet been filed but assured action once received.

The viral clip has raised serious questions over hygiene at roadside eateries, with locals demanding strict enforcement of food safety rules.
